items.html: And after their place was explained, we shall explain their names in the verses. And they are hinted at in "Who is a God like You, etc." and in "The Lord, the Lord, God, merciful and gracious, etc." And this is their meaning: 1, Who is a God like You; 2, Who pardons iniquity; 3, and passes over transgression; 4, for the remnant of His inheritance; 5, He does not retain His anger forever; 6, for He delights in mercy; 7, He will return and have compassion on us; 8, He will subdue our iniquities; 9, and You will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea; 10, You will give truth to Jacob; 11, mercy to Abraham; 12, which You have sworn to our fathers; 13, from the days of old. And corresponding to them are the thirteen attributes of "VaYa'avor," and they begin from "merciful and gracious" (El Rachum veChanun), as written in the Idra of Naso, page 131, side B: "corresponding to this, El Rachum veChanun, etc., and they are below." And in the explanation of the prayers this is well explained; see there. And part of it will be explained below.
